newsitem.title: USA: Shell ramps up Mars, Auger production.
newsitem.headline: Shell ramps up Mars, Auger production.

text.p: Shell Deepwater Production Inc said on Monday that production from the Mars deepwater platform in the U.S. Gulf has reached design capacity of 100,000 barrels of oil and 110 million cubic feet of natural gas a day.

The Mars tension leg platform has 11 wells in production and additional drilling is set to begin in September, with production rates set to rise in 1998 following debottlenecking procedures, Shell said.

The Mars platform, which began production in July 1996 in 2,940 feet of water, is operated by Shell, which has a 71.5 percent working interest. Shell is the U.S. unit of Anglo-Dutch Royal Dutch/Shell. British Petroleum Co Plc holds the remaining 28.5 percent interest.

Shell's Auger tension leg platform is producing at 100,000 barrels of oil and about 300 million cubic feet of gas per day following debottlenecking and expansions, the company said. The platform was originally designed to handle 46,000 barrels of oil and 125 million cubic feet of gas per day.

Auger, which was placed on production in 1994 in 2,860 feet of water, is producing from nine wells. The project is 100 percent owned by Shell Deepwater, part of Houston-based Shell Oil Co's exploration and production group.
